slides.title: Start with the patient
slides.section: Start with the patient
paragraphs: Infection? Compatible syndrome and a meaningful specimen.
Urgency? Shock, organ dysfunction, immune status.
Likely activity? Prior isolates, recent antibiotics, local data.
Source? Drain, remove, relieve obstruction; confirm drug exposure.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Start with the patient Infection? Compatible syndrome and a meaningful specimen. Urgency? Shock, organ dysfunction, immune status. Likely activity? Prior isolates, recent antibiotics, local data. Source? Drain, remove, relieve obstruction; confirm drug exposure. Reassessment? Review cultures, narrow, and set a stop plan. A resistant culture does not establish infection. A rectal CRE screen or a chronically positive tracheal aspirate may indicate colonization. Asymptomatic bacteriuria usually needs no antibiotic; pregnancy and endourologic procedures involving mucosal trauma are key exceptions. In severe infection, obtain appropriate cultures without delaying urgent therapy. Use the patient's prior organism and susceptibility results to choose empiric coverage. “History of MDRO” is less useful than “prior NDM-producing Klebsiella.” Request missing susceptibility tests early. First question for the room: What clinical evidence would make you treat this isolate? Sources amr , asb

slides.title: Susceptible does not mean interchangeable
slides.section: Read the organism, mechanism, and MIC together
paragraphs: Use the drug-specific breakpoint and infection site. A smaller MIC for another drug does not make it a better choice. SDD requires the exposure linked to that category; EUCAST “I” means susceptible with increased exposure.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Read the organism, mechanism, and MIC together Susceptible does not mean interchangeable Use the drug-specific breakpoint and infection site. A smaller MIC for another drug does not make it a better choice. SDD requires the exposure linked to that category; EUCAST “I” means susceptible with increased exposure. A gene result is a clue A detected carbapenemase can redirect therapy before full AST. A negative panel excludes only its targets. Multiple mechanisms may coexist; confirm the phenotype and test the intended drug. Two distinctions do most of the work today. ESBL and inducible AmpC differ in whether cefepime is a dependable choice. KPC, NDM, and OXA-48-like enzymes differ in which beta-lactamase inhibitor works. Do not read a matrix color as the patient's susceptibility result. AST means antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Check the isolate, site, dose, and current laboratory interpretation before prescribing. Sources amr , breakpoints , eucast

slides.section: Read the organism, mechanism, and MIC together
paragraphs: A detected carbapenemase can redirect therapy before full AST. A negative panel excludes only its targets. Multiple mechanisms may coexist; confirm the phenotype and test the intended drug.

slides.title: Use the matrix to connect resistance with treatment
slides.section: Use the matrix to connect resistance with treatment
paragraphs: Antibiotics run down the rows; resistance patterns run across the columns. This is a teaching synthesis for invasive infection, not a local antibiogram or a substitute for isolate-specific AST.

Green · S* Usually susceptible / expected activity. Confirm AST; not a guarantee or a preferred-drug ranking. Yellow · Caution Conditional use because of variable susceptibility, site, dosing, reserve status, or limited evidence. Red · R / Avoid R = expected resistance or no useful activity. Avoid = clinically unreliable or not suggested, even if reported susceptible.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Use the matrix to connect resistance with treatment Antibiotics run down the rows; resistance patterns run across the columns. This is a teaching synthesis for invasive infection, not a local antibiogram or a substitute for isolate-specific AST. Green · S* Usually susceptible / expected activity. Confirm AST; not a guarantee or a preferred-drug ranking. Yellow · Caution Conditional use because of variable susceptibility, site, dosing, reserve status, or limited evidence. Red · R / Avoid R = expected resistance or no useful activity. Avoid = clinically unreliable or not suggested, even if reported susceptible. “Reserve” means activity may be present, but preserve the drug for more resistant infections. Non-beta-lactam susceptibility cannot be inferred from an ESBL or carbapenemase label. A blank qualifier never waives AST. Gram-negative resistance patterns Antibiotic ESBL-E Inducible AmpC-E KPC-E NDM-E OXA-48-like-E DTR Pseudomonas Ceftriaxone R Avoid Induction R R Avoid Unreliable R Piperacillin–tazobactam Avoid Invasive disease Avoid Invasive disease R R R R Cefepime Avoid ESBL disease S* Optimize dose R R Avoid Unreliable R Meropenem / imipenem–cilastatin S* S* R R Avoid Unreliable R Ertapenem Caution Not critical illness S* R R R R Ceftolozane–tazobactam Caution Reserve Avoid AmpC R R R Caution AST; no MBL Ceftazidime–avibactam Caution Reserve Caution Reserve S* R NDM alone S* Caution AST; no MBL Meropenem–vaborbactam Caution Reserve Caution Reserve S* R Avoid Inhibitor mismatch Avoid No added benefit Imipenem–cilastatin–relebactam Caution Reserve Caution Reserve S* R Avoid Inhibitor mismatch Caution AST; no MBL Aztreonam–avibactam Caution Reserve Caution Reserve Caution Alternative S* Confirm AST Caution Alternative Avoid Limited activity Cefiderocol Caution Reserve Caution Reserve Caution Alternative S* Confirm AST Caution Alternative Caution AST; MBL option TMP–SMX Caution AST; site Caution AST; site Caution AST; site Caution AST; site Caution AST; site R Levofloxacin Caution AST; site Caution AST; site Caution AST; site Caution AST; site Caution AST; site R E = Enterobacterales. AmpC column assumes a species at moderate risk for inducible AmpC, without an additional ESBL or carbapenemase. DTR = nonsusceptible to the usual antipseudomonal beta-lactams and fluoroquinolones. MBL = metallo-beta-lactamase. The NDM-E column does not apply to MBL-producing Pseudomonas. Recognize these three patterns ESBL versus AmpC — For invasive ESBL, start with a carbapenem. For susceptible inducible AmpC, optimized cefepime is a key option. Moderate-risk species include E. cloacae complex, K. aerogenes, C. freundii, and H. alvei. Match the CRE inhibitor — KPC has several active inhibitor combinations; NDM requires aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol; OXA-48-like favors ceftazidime-avibactam. NDM can coexist with enzymes that destroy aztreonam alone. DTR Pseudomonas — Request AST for ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, and cefiderocol. For MBL producers, cefiderocol is the preferred option if active. slides.title: Bladder versus kidney or blood
slides.section: The source changes the treatment
paragraphs: Nitrofurantoin is not a pyelonephritis or bloodstream drug. Oral fosfomycin is not initial treatment for pyelonephritis or sepsis and is not routine bloodstream therapy. A selected transition after active IV treatment for improving E. coli complicated UTI is a separate use discussed in the antibiotic primer . Oral transition for invasive infection requires an active drug with adequate systemic exposure.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
The source changes the treatment Bladder versus kidney or blood Nitrofurantoin is not a pyelonephritis or bloodstream drug. Oral fosfomycin is not initial treatment for pyelonephritis or sepsis and is not routine bloodstream therapy. A selected transition after active IV treatment for improving E. coli complicated UTI is a separate use discussed in the antibiotic primer . Oral transition for invasive infection requires an active drug with adequate systemic exposure. Lung versus blood Daptomycin can treat bacteremia but not alveolar pneumonia. A respiratory CRAB or Stenotrophomonas isolate needs a compatible syndrome before treatment. The matrix cannot distinguish a colonizer from the cause of pneumonia. Exposure and toxicity Match dose and infusion to the MIC, site, and renal function. Cefepime accumulation can cause neurotoxicity. Monitor potassium, renal function, and CBC with TMP-SMX; CBC with linezolid; CK with daptomycin. Use pharmacy support for vancomycin and complex dosing. Control the source, then narrow Drain collections, relieve obstruction, and address infected devices. Persistent infection warrants a source and exposure review plus repeat susceptibility testing when appropriate. Stop redundant coverage once a reliable active regimen is established; use combinations when there is a specific rationale. Resistance alone does not determine duration. slides.title: Case 1 · An ESBL bloodstream isolate
slides.section: Use three cases to practice treatment decisions
paragraphs: A patient with E. coli bacteremia from obstructed pyelonephritis is hypotensive. The isolate is ESBL-producing and reported susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam.
What determines the immediate drug and the source intervention?
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Use three cases to practice treatment decisions Case 1 · An ESBL bloodstream isolate A patient with E. coli bacteremia from obstructed pyelonephritis is hypotensive. The isolate is ESBL-producing and reported susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam. What determines the immediate drug and the source intervention? Reveal teaching point Use meropenem or imipenem-cilastatin if active and urgently relieve the obstruction. A susceptible piperacillin-tazobactam result does not make it the preferred treatment for ESBL bacteremia. After stability and source control, consider an active oral systemic agent when appropriate, not nitrofurantoin. Case 2 · Ceftriaxone-susceptible Enterobacter E. cloacae complex grows in blood. Ceftriaxone and cefepime are reported susceptible. Why is ceftriaxone susceptibility not the end of the decision? Reveal teaching point Inducible AmpC can emerge during treatment. For invasive infection, optimized cefepime is an appropriate option if active and no other mechanism undermines it. Use a carbapenem when indicated by severity, susceptibility, or coexisting ESBL. Check source control and the delivered dose. Case 3 · A carbapenemase result changes the plan K. pneumoniae bacteremia is initially treated with ceftazidime-avibactam. The rapid assay detects NDM. What should change before the complete susceptibility panel returns? Reveal teaching point Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not cover NDM. Promptly choose a mechanism-appropriate regimen guided by prior AST and local access, then confirm current AST. Preferred options are aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative if the fixed combination is unavailable. Do not transfer this algorithm to MBL Pseudomonas. Sources amr

slides.title: Begin with five clinical decisions before choosing a drug
slides.section: Begin with five clinical decisions before choosing a drug
paragraphs: Is this infection? Name the syndrome and assess specimen quality.
How urgent is it? Assess shock, organ dysfunction, and immune status.
What is likely active? Review prior isolates, recent therapy, and the local antibiogram.
Will it reach the site? Check tissue exposure, dose, route, and source control.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Begin with five clinical decisions before choosing a drug Is this infection? Name the syndrome and assess specimen quality. How urgent is it? Assess shock, organ dysfunction, and immune status. What is likely active? Review prior isolates, recent therapy, and the local antibiogram. Will it reach the site? Check tissue exposure, dose, route, and source control. What changes tomorrow? Set a culture review, narrowing plan, and monitoring plan. A resistant organism in urine, a chronic wound, or a tracheal aspirate may be colonization. A new compatible syndrome, objective findings, and the quality of the specimen determine whether treatment is warranted. A rectal CRE screen guides precautions and empiric risk assessment; it is not an indication for antibiotics. Obtain appropriate cultures before antibiotics when feasible without delaying urgent treatment. In severe infection, use prior organism and susceptibility results, recent antibiotic exposure, the likely source, and current local epidemiology to select initial coverage. Prior NDM or KPC infection can change the first drug; a generic history of “MDRO” is insufficient. Ask microbiology to retain invasive isolates and test additional agents early. Reassess when identification and susceptibility results return. Stop unnecessary MRSA or double gram-negative coverage. A drained collection, relieved urinary obstruction, removed infected catheter, or revised infected device may matter more than adding another antibiotic. Do not treat an asymptomatic culture Asymptomatic bacteriuria generally does not need antibiotics, including when the isolate is ESBL-producing or VRE. Established indications include pregnancy and before endoscopic urologic procedures involving mucosal trauma. Pyuria alone does not distinguish infection from colonization. Severe systemic illness requires a clinical evaluation, not automatic dismissal as asymptomatic bacteriuria. Sources amr , asb , cdc

slides.title: Mechanisms explain which apparently similar drugs are different
slides.section: Mechanisms explain which apparently similar drugs are different
rows: ESBLs, AmpC, KPC, NDM, OXA enzymes
The inhibitor must match the enzyme. Ceftazidime-avibactam activity against KPC does not imply activity against NDM.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Mechanisms explain which apparently similar drugs are different Resistance mechanisms and clinical consequences Mechanism Examples What changes at the bedside Drug destruction ESBLs, AmpC, KPC, NDM, OXA enzymes The inhibitor must match the enzyme. Ceftazidime-avibactam activity against KPC does not imply activity against NDM. Altered target mecA/mecC and altered penicillin-binding proteins; van genes; gyrase mutations MRSA resists usual antistaphylococcal beta-lactams. Vancomycin resistance does not independently establish ampicillin or daptomycin resistance. Reduced entry Porin loss, including OprD in Pseudomonas Carbapenem resistance can coexist with cefepime susceptibility. Not every carbapenem-resistant isolate produces a carbapenemase. Active drug efflux Pseudomonas and Stenotrophomonas efflux systems Multiple classes can be affected; a single enzyme result cannot fully predict the phenotype. Multiple mechanisms together ESBL or AmpC plus porin loss; NDM plus other beta-lactamases A phenotype may require more than one explanation. Repeat susceptibility testing when infection recurs after treatment. Intrinsic resistance and biofilm are different problems Enterococci are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporin monotherapy. Ertapenem does not cover Pseudomonas or Acinetobacter. Stenotrophomonas is intrinsically resistant to carbapenems. Biofilm-associated persistence may occur despite a susceptible MIC because routine testing evaluates planktonic organisms; investigate the infected surface or device. ESBL and AmpC describe beta-lactamases. CRE describes a resistance phenotype or carbapenemase production. KPC and NDM identify mechanisms. MDR describes resistance across several categories. DTR Pseudomonas means nonsusceptibility to all eight traditional agents listed in the Pseudomonas section. These terms are related but not interchangeable. Sources amr , mrsa , breakpoints

slides.title: Intrinsic resistance and biofilm are different problems
slides.section: Mechanisms explain which apparently similar drugs are different
paragraphs: Enterococci are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporin monotherapy. Ertapenem does not cover Pseudomonas or Acinetobacter. Stenotrophomonas is intrinsically resistant to carbapenems. Biofilm-associated persistence may occur despite a susceptible MIC because routine testing evaluates planktonic organisms; investigate the infected surface or device.

slides.title: Read the susceptibility report as a conditional prediction
slides.section: Read the susceptibility report as a conditional prediction
rows: A lower MIC for drug A than drug B
MIC numbers across different antibiotics are not a potency ranking. Breakpoints and achievable exposures differ.
Compare each result with the applicable organism, site, and dosing breakpoint.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Read the susceptibility report as a conditional prediction Interpretation pitfalls Report Interpretation Action A lower MIC for drug A than drug B MIC numbers across different antibiotics are not a potency ranking. Breakpoints and achievable exposures differ. Compare each result with the applicable organism, site, and dosing breakpoint. Susceptible dose-dependent (SDD) The category assumes a specified higher exposure. It is not standard-dose susceptibility. Ask which regimen supports the result. Cefepime MIC 4-8 micrograms/mL in Enterobacterales is SDD under the cited 2026 criteria. EUCAST “I” EUCAST defines I as susceptible with increased exposure. It is not interchangeable with the CLSI intermediate category. Confirm which standard your laboratory uses before interpreting an outside report. CTX-M detected Supports an ESBL mechanism in the relevant organism. Use an ESBL-informed regimen while awaiting the full phenotype. A negative CTX-M result does not exclude other ESBLs or AmpC. Carbapenemase panel negative Only the targets on that panel were excluded. Porin/efflux mechanisms and untested enzymes remain possible. Reconcile with the phenotype; obtain broader phenotypic or reference-laboratory testing for discordance. Drug not listed May reflect selective reporting, no routine test, or lack of validated breakpoints. Ask for the actual MIC, method, interpretation, and additional testing. Do not assume susceptibility or resistance. Susceptible but poor site exposure In vitro activity is insufficient if exposure at the infected site is inadequate. Avoid nitrofurantoin for pyelonephritis or bacteremia and daptomycin for alveolar pneumonia. For presumed ESBL in E. coli, K. pneumoniae, or K. oxytoca, the 2026 IDSA document uses ceftriaxone MIC at least 4 micrograms/mL as a surrogate. This is not molecular confirmation and is not a universal rule for every Enterobacterales species. In mixed cultures, confirm which organism carries a detected resistance gene. Ask specifically about newer beta-lactam testing for CRE or DTR Pseudomonas, combination testing when using ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam, and reliable cefiderocol testing. A breakpoint for one species or formulation must not be borrowed for another. Oral and IV fosfomycin have different interpretive criteria. Sources amr , breakpoints , eucast

slides.title: Treat ESBL infection according to the site and severity
slides.section: Treat ESBL infection according to the site and severity
rows: Nitrofurantoin or TMP-SMX when active and appropriate. The 2026 guidance also includes single-dose aminoglycoside, gepotidacin, pivmecillinam, and oral sulopenem-probenecid among preferred options.
Check patient eligibility, availability, interactions, and susceptibility. Fosfomycin is an alternative for E. coli cystitis. Do not extrapolate a bladder regimen to febrile or invasive disease.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Treat ESBL infection according to the site and severity ESBL treatment by syndrome Syndrome Practical choice Important limits Bladder-only infection Nitrofurantoin or TMP-SMX when active and appropriate. The 2026 guidance also includes single-dose aminoglycoside, gepotidacin, pivmecillinam, and oral sulopenem-probenecid among preferred options. Check patient eligibility, availability, interactions, and susceptibility. Fosfomycin is an alternative for E. coli cystitis. Do not extrapolate a bladder regimen to febrile or invasive disease. Pyelonephritis / cUTI Susceptible TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin. If unsuitable, a carbapenem or cefepime-enmetazobactam. IV fosfomycin, aminoglycosides, and piperacillin-tazobactam are alternatives in the 2026 guidance. Bacteremia or critical illness favors the invasive-disease approach. Bacteremia, pneumonia, or other invasive infection A carbapenem is preferred. Use meropenem or imipenem-cilastatin in critical illness or hypoalbuminemia. Ertapenem can be useful in stable patients with appropriate pharmacokinetics and source control. Cefepime-enmetazobactam is an alternative; invasive ESBL outcome data are less established. Oral transition after improvement Active TMP-SMX or a fluoroquinolone, after hemodynamic stability, source control, and confirmation of absorption. For bloodstream infection, do not use nitrofurantoin or oral fosfomycin as completion therapy. An ESBL label does not itself mandate a PICC. Avoid plain cefepime for ESBL pyelonephritis/cUTI or invasive disease even when it reports susceptible. Cefepime-enmetazobactam is a distinct combination with a different role. Piperacillin-tazobactam is not preferred for ESBL bacteremia; MERINO failed to establish noninferiority to meropenem. Fosfomycin needs a formulation and a site Oral fosfomycin is principally a cystitis option for E. coli. The 2026 guidance permits selected oral transition use after initial improvement in E. coli cUTI when other oral options are unavailable, with limited supporting evidence. This is not initial therapy for pyelonephritis, nor reliable bacteremia therapy. IV fosfomycin is a separate alternative for cUTI with different dosing, susceptibility criteria, and sodium burden. Sources amr , merino , allium , breakpoints

slides.section: Species-level identification helps predict resistance emerging during treatment
paragraphs: Enterobacter cloacae complex, Klebsiella aerogenes, and Citrobacter freundii have clinically important inducible AmpC risk. The 2026 guidance adds Hafnia alvei, supported mainly by laboratory data and limited clinical experience. A ceftriaxone-susceptible initial isolate can become resistant during therapy.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Species-level identification helps predict resistance emerging during treatment Enterobacter cloacae complex, Klebsiella aerogenes, and Citrobacter freundii have clinically important inducible AmpC risk. The 2026 guidance adds Hafnia alvei, supported mainly by laboratory data and limited clinical experience. A ceftriaxone-susceptible initial isolate can become resistant during therapy. For invasive infection, cefepime is a reasonable definitive option when susceptible or SDD and dosed to the required exposure. A carbapenem is appropriate when cefepime is inactive, ESBL co-production is established, or the clinical situation makes cefepime unreliable. Piperacillin-tazobactam is not suggested for invasive infection from these moderate-risk organisms. Do not apply an old “SPICE” mnemonic uniformly. Serratia marcescens, Morganella morganii, and Providencia species have a lower likelihood of clinically significant AmpC overexpression; generally follow susceptibility testing. In high-burden infection or inadequate source control, cefepime may still be preferred. C. koseri is not C. freundii, and K. pneumoniae is not K. aerogenes. Nuance without losing the default Avoid ceftriaxone as the planned treatment of invasive moderate-risk AmpC infection. The 2026 guidance allows completion with empiric ceftriaxone in selected non-severe infections after clear improvement and adequate source control. This exception should not justify ceftriaxone in shock, an undrained collection, or an endovascular infection. Sources amr , breakpoints

paragraphs: Avoid ceftriaxone as the planned treatment of invasive moderate-risk AmpC infection. The 2026 guidance allows completion with empiric ceftriaxone in selected non-severe infections after clear improvement and adequate source control. This exception should not justify ceftriaxone in shock, an undrained collection, or an endovascular infection.
Sources amr , breakpoints
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Species-level identification helps predict resistance emerging during treatment Enterobacter cloacae complex, Klebsiella aerogenes, and Citrobacter freundii have clinically important inducible AmpC risk. The 2026 guidance adds Hafnia alvei, supported mainly by laboratory data and limited clinical experience. A ceftriaxone-susceptible initial isolate can become resistant during therapy. For invasive infection, cefepime is a reasonable definitive option when susceptible or SDD and dosed to the required exposure. A carbapenem is appropriate when cefepime is inactive, ESBL co-production is established, or the clinical situation makes cefepime unreliable. Piperacillin-tazobactam is not suggested for invasive infection from these moderate-risk organisms. Do not apply an old “SPICE” mnemonic uniformly. Serratia marcescens, Morganella morganii, and Providencia species have a lower likelihood of clinically significant AmpC overexpression; generally follow susceptibility testing. In high-burden infection or inadequate source control, cefepime may still be preferred. C. koseri is not C. freundii, and K. pneumoniae is not K. aerogenes. Nuance without losing the default Avoid ceftriaxone as the planned treatment of invasive moderate-risk AmpC infection. The 2026 guidance allows completion with empiric ceftriaxone in selected non-severe infections after clear improvement and adequate source control. This exception should not justify ceftriaxone in shock, an undrained collection, or an endovascular infection. Sources amr , breakpoints

slides.title: For CRE, identify the carbapenemase before assuming the new drugs are interchangeable
slides.section: For CRE, identify the carbapenemase before assuming the new drugs are interchangeable
rows: Meropenem-vaborbactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, or imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam. IDSA slightly favors meropenem-vaborbactam within this group.
This preference is not based on a head-to-head randomized trial. Prior exposure and new MICs matter.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
For CRE, identify the carbapenemase before assuming the new drugs are interchangeable Definitive therapy for invasive CRE with demonstrated activity Mechanism or phenotype Preferred approach Avoid the shortcut KPC Meropenem-vaborbactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, or imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam. IDSA slightly favors meropenem-vaborbactam within this group. This preference is not based on a head-to-head randomized trial. Prior exposure and new MICs matter. NDM / other metallo-beta-lactamase For NDM, aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. If aztreonam-avibactam is unavailable, ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative. For VIM/IMP, confirm organism-specific testing and specialist interpretation. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone, meropenem-vaborbactam, and imipenem-relebactam do not solve an MBL mechanism. OXA-48-like Ceftazidime-avibactam preferred; cefiderocol or aztreonam-avibactam are alternatives. Vaborbactam and relebactam do not reliably inhibit OXA-48-like enzymes, even if an isolated susceptible report appears reassuring. No carbapenemase; ertapenem nonsusceptible but meropenem and imipenem susceptible IDSA exposure-optimized meropenem or imipenem-cilastatin, with close follow-up; coordinate any departure from local standard infusion with pharmacy. Ertapenem resistance alone does not mean all carbapenems are inactive. No carbapenemase; all carbapenems nonsusceptible A susceptible newer beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor, selected with microbiology and ID. Do not escalate the dose of an inactive carbapenem and presume the resistance is overcome. Aztreonam survives MBL hydrolysis, but co-produced serine beta-lactamases can destroy it. Avibactam protects aztreonam from those accompanying enzymes. Avibactam does not inhibit NDM itself. This explains why the combination can work when aztreonam alone and ceftazidime-avibactam alone do not. Do not routinely add an aminoglycoside or polymyxin once an active beta-lactam regimen is established. Tigecycline and eravacycline are alternatives only for suitable nonbloodstream, nonurinary sites. They are poor choices for CRE bacteremia or UTI. Guidance use and the US label are not identical The retrieved US aztreonam-avibactam label is for adults with limited or no alternatives who have complicated intra-abdominal infection, with concurrent metronidazole. IDSA-supported use for NDM bacteremia and other sites extends beyond that label. Do not describe all CRE uses as FDA-approved. Sources amr , emblaveo

slides.title: Carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas does not automatically require a reserve antibiotic
slides.section: Carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas does not automatically require a reserve antibiotic
paragraphs: If cefepime, ceftazidime, piperacillin-tazobactam, or aztreonam remains susceptible, an optimized traditional beta-lactam may be appropriate even when carbapenems are resistant. In critical illness or poor source control, a susceptible newer agent is also reasonable. OprD loss can disproportionately affect carbapenems; this is one reason to interpret the complete pattern.

DTR Pseudomonas is nonsusceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam, ceftazidime, cefepime, aztreonam, meropenem, imipenem, ciprofloxacin, and levofloxacin. Request testing of ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, and cefiderocol.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas does not automatically require a reserve antibiotic If cefepime, ceftazidime, piperacillin-tazobactam, or aztreonam remains susceptible, an optimized traditional beta-lactam may be appropriate even when carbapenems are resistant. In critical illness or poor source control, a susceptible newer agent is also reasonable. OprD loss can disproportionately affect carbapenems; this is one reason to interpret the complete pattern. DTR Pseudomonas is nonsusceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam, ceftazidime, cefepime, aztreonam, meropenem, imipenem, ciprofloxacin, and levofloxacin. Request testing of ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, and cefiderocol. DTR Pseudomonas by clinical context Context Treatment approach Infection outside the urinary tract Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, or imipenem-relebactam when active. Cefiderocol is an alternative. Pneumonia The 2026 guidance favors ceftolozane-tazobactam among the preferred agents when susceptible. The comparative evidence does not establish universal superiority across all sites. cUTI All four newer agents are preferred options when active. Once-daily amikacin or tobramycin may be alternatives with pharmacokinetic monitoring. MBL-producing Pseudomonas Cefiderocol preferred when susceptible. Aztreonam-avibactam has limited activity here; do not transfer the NDM Enterobacterales algorithm to Pseudomonas. Recurrence after a newer beta-lactam Obtain new cultures and repeat susceptibility testing. Cross-resistance can emerge, including between ceftolozane-tazobactam and ceftazidime-avibactam. Once a beta-lactam is confirmed active, routine continued combination therapy is not suggested. Aminoglycoside monotherapy is unsuitable for invasive nonurinary disease. Routine adjunctive inhaled antibiotics are not recommended when an active systemic beta-lactam is available. Sources amr

slides.title: For invasive CRAB, use a sulbactam-durlobactam regimen and verify that the isolate is causing disease
slides.section: For invasive CRAB, use a sulbactam-durlobactam regimen and verify that the isolate is causing disease
paragraphs: CRAB means carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex. A positive respiratory or wound culture is often difficult to interpret. Establish a compatible infection before exposing a patient to a complex regimen.

Preferred treatment is sulbactam-durlobactam plus imipenem-cilastatin or meropenem. Sulbactam has direct antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter; durlobactam protects it from relevant beta-lactamases. The carbapenem is an intentional partner in this regimen, not evidence that carbapenem monotherapy is effective against CRAB.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
For invasive CRAB, use a sulbactam-durlobactam regimen and verify that the isolate is causing disease CRAB means carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex. A positive respiratory or wound culture is often difficult to interpret. Establish a compatible infection before exposing a patient to a complex regimen. Preferred treatment is sulbactam-durlobactam plus imipenem-cilastatin or meropenem. Sulbactam has direct antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter; durlobactam protects it from relevant beta-lactamases. The carbapenem is an intentional partner in this regimen, not evidence that carbapenem monotherapy is effective against CRAB. The 2026 guidance places high-dose ampicillin-sulbactam plus another active agent in a temporary bridging role when sulbactam-durlobactam is not immediately available. The target is 9 g/day of the sulbactam component, equal to 27 g/day of the fixed ampicillin-sulbactam product before renal adjustment. Arrange access to preferred therapy rather than assuming these regimens are equivalent. If sulbactam-durlobactam resistance or an MBL is identified, obtain specialist guidance for a nonsulbactam combination using available active agents such as cefiderocol, minocycline, or polymyxin B. The optimal salvage regimen is uncertain. Do not generalize OXA-48 Enterobacterales treatment to Acinetobacter OXA carbapenemases. What ATTACK established Sulbactam-durlobactam plus imipenem-cilastatin met a prespecified noninferiority endpoint against colistin plus imipenem-cilastatin, with substantially less nephrotoxicity. The mortality confidence interval included no difference. The study does not establish a mortality superiority claim, and most patients had pneumonia. Sources amr , attack , doses

slides.title: Stenotrophomonas treatment requires an explicit assessment of the evidence
slides.section: Stenotrophomonas treatment requires an explicit assessment of the evidence
paragraphs: First determine whether a respiratory isolate represents infection. Carbapenem exposure can select Stenotrophomonas, and meropenem does not treat it. Invasive disease includes clinically established pneumonia, bloodstream infection, and other deep infection; a positive airway culture alone is insufficient.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Stenotrophomonas treatment requires an explicit assessment of the evidence First determine whether a respiratory isolate represents infection. Carbapenem exposure can select Stenotrophomonas, and meropenem does not treat it. Invasive disease includes clinically established pneumonia, bloodstream infection, and other deep infection; a positive airway culture alone is insufficient. A substantive 2026 change The 2026 IDSA guidance favors cefiderocol monotherapy for invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infection. slides.title: MRSA and VRE require different treatment decisions at different infection sites
slides.section: MRSA and VRE require different treatment decisions at different infection sites
rows: Vancomycin or daptomycin are established options. Ceftobiprole is another option for adult S. aureus bacteremia within its approved indication; assess availability and trial applicability.
Follow-up cultures, source control, evaluation for endocarditis and metastatic infection, and a syndrome-specific duration.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
MRSA and VRE require different treatment decisions at different infection sites Resistant gram-positive organisms Organism and site Treatment framework What must accompany the drug MRSA bacteremia / endovascular infection Vancomycin or daptomycin are established options. Ceftobiprole is another option for adult S. aureus bacteremia within its approved indication; assess availability and trial applicability. Follow-up cultures, source control, evaluation for endocarditis and metastatic infection, and a syndrome-specific duration. MRSA alveolar pneumonia Vancomycin or linezolid. Daptomycin is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant. Drain empyema when present. Oral bioavailability alone does not establish suitability for an unstable patient. Purulent MRSA skin infection Drain an abscess; add a susceptible oral agent such as TMP-SMX or doxycycline when systemic treatment is indicated, or IV therapy for severe disease. If accompanying nonpurulent cellulitis needs streptococcal coverage, ensure the regimen provides it. Clindamycin requires attention to inducible resistance testing. VRE E. faecium bacteremia Linezolid or high-dose daptomycin selected by susceptibility, site, organ function, and toxicity. Daptomycin use for VRE is off-label. Confirm species, actual daptomycin MIC, source control, and clearance. A usual S. aureus daptomycin dose of 6 mg/kg is not the default for serious VRE infection. Vancomycin-resistant but ampicillin-susceptible enterococcus Ampicillin may remain useful; an endovascular infection needs a syndrome-specific regimen. Vancomycin resistance does not rule out all beta-lactams. Cephalosporin monotherapy does not treat enterococci. VRE in urine without symptoms Usually no antibiotic. Apply the asymptomatic bacteriuria framework. For symptomatic cystitis, consider a susceptible urinary agent; for pyelonephritis or bacteremia, use systemic therapy. For E. faecium, a daptomycin MIC at most 4 micrograms/mL is CLSI susceptible dose-dependent, tied to 8-12 mg/kg/day exposure; this is not an FDA-approved VRE dosing indication. An MIC of 4 in another enterococcal species has a different interpretation. Confirm the laboratory standard before prescribing. FDA discussion of CLSI criteria . For serious MRSA infection, national vancomycin guidance favors AUC-guided dosing, generally AUC24/MIC 400-600 when MIC is assumed to be 1 mg/L. Some services use pharmacy-directed trough monitoring. Confirm the treating service’s approach, target, draw timing, and creatinine monitoring; do not equate a single trough with an AUC. For S. aureus bacteremia, the September 2026 IDSA/ESCMID consensus emphasizes risk stratification and diagnostic evaluation. Adults without deep or metastatic foci after appropriate evaluation generally receive 14 days; persistent bacteremia or an incomplete evaluation can justify longer therapy. Endocarditis, osteomyelitis, and retained infected devices require their own plans. Do not prescribe 4-6 weeks solely because the isolate is MRSA. Persistent bacteremia is a diagnostic problem as well as a treatment problem Reassess lines, valves, devices, undrained collections, dosing, and repeat susceptibilities. Daptomycin plus a beta-lactam may be considered as specialist salvage for selected persistent MRSA or VRE infections. Routine upfront combination therapy is not established for every patient; the partner beta-lactam may be intended for synergy rather than independent susceptibility. slides.section: Dose and infusion strategy are part of whether the regimen is active
paragraphs: National exposure examples and local administration: the table below includes IDSA prolonged-infusion regimens. These examples are not an order set; infusion methods and access vary by institution. If a susceptibility interpretation or resistant-organism regimen depends on optimized exposure, resolve the dose and administration with ID pharmacy before prescribing. Confirm the treating service’s vancomycin monitoring method with pharmacy.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Dose and infusion strategy are part of whether the regimen is active National exposure examples and local administration: the table below includes IDSA prolonged-infusion regimens. These examples are not an order set; infusion methods and access vary by institution. If a susceptibility interpretation or resistant-organism regimen depends on optimized exposure, resolve the dose and administration with ID pharmacy before prescribing. Confirm the treating service’s vancomycin monitoring method with pharmacy. Examples below are for adults with normal organ function and the stated infection context. They are not renal-replacement, CNS, pediatric, or pregnancy dosing tables. Recalculate exposure with changing renal function, obesity, augmented clearance, and extracorporeal support. Pharmacy should confirm the exact product components and administration plan. Selected adult regimens requiring careful prescribing Agent / context Example regimen Practical check Cefepime, invasive AmpC or susceptible Pseudomonas 2 g IV loading dose over 30 minutes, then 2 g every 8 hours over 3 hours. Renal adjustment; encephalopathy, myoclonus, or seizures may be toxicity. Meropenem, invasive gram-negative disease 1-2 g IV every 8 hours, prolonged infusion over 3 hours when feasible. Choose exposure for site, MIC, and clearance. Severe or selected high-exposure contexts often use 2 g. Meropenem-vaborbactam 4 g total IV every 8 hours over 3 hours. Contains 2 g of each component; adjust for renal function. Ceftazidime-avibactam 2.5 g total IV every 8 hours over 3 hours in IDSA guidance. If paired with aztreonam, pharmacy coordinates simultaneous infusion; this is not interchangeable with the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product. Aztreonam-avibactam 2.67 g total loading dose, then 2 g total every 6 hours; infuse each over 3 hours. Maintenance contains 1.5 g aztreonam plus 0.5 g avibactam. Renal adjustment; add metronidazole for intra-abdominal anaerobic coverage. Ceftolozane-tazobactam, invasive DTR infection 3 g total IV every 8 hours over 3 hours. Contains 2 g ceftolozane plus 1 g tazobactam; distinguish from lower-dose bladder regimens. Cefiderocol 2 g IV every 8 hours over 3 hours. For creatinine clearance at least 120 mL/min, the cited guidance uses every 6 hours; reduced renal function also changes dosing. Sulbactam-durlobactam 2 g total IV every 6 hours over 3 hours, with a carbapenem partner. Contains 1 g of each component; at creatinine clearance at least 130 mL/min, every 4 hours. Use the full label for other renal strata. Linezolid 600 mg IV or orally every 12 hours. CBC at least weekly; interactions, neuropathy and lactic acidosis with longer use. Renal dysfunction increases hematologic toxicity risk. Daptomycin, serious VRE infection Common specialist dosing is 10-12 mg/kg IV every 24 hours before renal adjustment. Confirm MIC and dosing weight with pharmacy; CK at baseline and at least weekly, more often with risk factors. Assess myalgia and new pulmonary symptoms. TMP-SMX, invasive Stenotrophomonas alternative regimen Dose by trimethoprim, not total tablet weight; individualize with pharmacy using the linked dosing table. Check K+, creatinine, CBC, renal adjustment, and interactions. Do not silently substitute a cystitis dose for invasive disease. For prolonged infusions, avoid a delay in achieving initial therapeutic exposure. Confirm loading-dose strategy, line access, compatibility, and infusion stability. Do not copy an inpatient infusion schedule into OPAT without verifying that the pump, preparation, and home administration can deliver it. slides.section: Work from the syndrome to a defensible treatment plan
paragraphs: Confirm the laboratory interpretation and source. Do not use a low S. aureus dose simply because the report is SDD. slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Work from the syndrome to a defensible treatment plan Pause before opening each discussion. Name the next action, drug choice, and information still missing. Case 1 · A resistant urine culture without symptoms A stable adult with a chronic urinary catheter has ESBL E. coli in urine obtained for odor. There is no new urinary symptom, fever, hemodynamic change, or planned invasive urologic procedure. Discuss the decision Do not treat the culture. Review why it was collected and whether the catheter is needed. Resistance does not convert asymptomatic bacteriuria into infection. Sources asb Case 2 · ESBL bacteremia with a susceptible piperacillin-tazobactam report A patient with fever, hypotension, an obstructing ureteral stone, and E. coli bacteremia has CTX-M detected. Piperacillin-tazobactam is reported susceptible. Discuss the decision Use an active carbapenem while arranging urgent urinary decompression. Once stable with source control and complete results, assess an active oral option. The susceptibility report does not negate the invasive ESBL treatment evidence. Sources merino Case 3 · Enterobacter initially susceptible to ceftriaxone E. cloacae complex grows from blood and an undrained intra-abdominal collection. Ceftriaxone is susceptible; cefepime MIC is 2 micrograms/mL. Discuss the decision Arrange drainage and select cefepime with appropriate exposure, or a carbapenem when indicated by clinical or resistance factors. Include anaerobic coverage if the source requires it. This is not the low-severity, source-controlled exception for continuing ceftriaxone. Sources amr Case 4 · NDM changes the CRE choice A bloodstream K. pneumoniae isolate carries NDM. Ceftazidime-avibactam was started before molecular results. Discuss the decision Ceftazidime-avibactam alone is inadequate. Select aztreonam-avibactam or susceptible cefiderocol; ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative if the fixed product is unavailable. Obtain confirmatory AST and source control. Sources amr Case 5 · Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas still has an older option A stable patient with a drained source has Pseudomonas resistant to meropenem but susceptible to cefepime. Discuss the decision Optimized cefepime can be appropriate. Carbapenem resistance is not synonymous with DTR or a carbapenemase. Check the MIC, exposure, source, and response; do not automatically escalate to a reserve agent. Sources amr Case 6 · CRAB in a ventilated patient New fever, purulent secretions, a new infiltrate, and rising oxygen requirements accompany a CRAB respiratory isolate. Discuss the decision Evaluate competing causes and specimen quality. If CRAB pneumonia is established, use sulbactam-durlobactam plus a carbapenem partner and request AST. A prior positive respiratory culture without this syndrome would not justify the same treatment. Sources amr Case 7 · Stenotrophomonas after broad-spectrum therapy A neutropenic patient has compatible pneumonia and S. maltophilia in blood and respiratory cultures. Discuss the decision Treat invasive disease promptly with the current guidance-informed approach, favoring active cefiderocol. Assess catheter and pulmonary sources. Explain that this recommendation is not supported by a definitive human superiority trial; alternatives require careful combination and toxicity planning. Sources amr Case 8 · VRE with daptomycin MIC 4 A patient has VRE E. faecium bacteremia, daptomycin MIC 4 micrograms/mL, and preserved renal function. Discuss the decision Confirm the laboratory interpretation and source. Do not use a low S. aureus dose simply because the report is SDD. Discuss high-dose daptomycin or linezolid, CBC/CK monitoring, clearance cultures, and endovascular evaluation when indicated. Persistent infection requires source and repeat-MIC reassessment. slides.title: Use these questions to check the reasoning
slides.section: Use these questions to check the reasoning
paragraphs: 1. Does the smallest MIC identify the best antibiotic?
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Use these questions to check the reasoning 1. Does the smallest MIC identify the best antibiotic? Show explanation No. Compare the drug-specific breakpoint, achievable exposure, site, and outcomes evidence. 2. Does a negative CTX-M result exclude ESBL? Show explanation No. Other ESBL families and other resistance mechanisms can produce a similar phenotype. 3. Which Enterobacterales should make you question ceftriaxone despite initial susceptibility? Show explanation E. cloacae complex, K. aerogenes, C. freundii, and, in the 2026 guidance, H. alvei. Severity and source control determine whether the limited continuation exception applies. 4. Why can aztreonam-avibactam work against NDM? Show explanation Aztreonam resists MBL hydrolysis; avibactam blocks accompanying serine beta-lactamases. Avibactam does not inhibit NDM. 5. Can you use the NDM Enterobacterales algorithm for MBL Pseudomonas? Show explanation No. Cefiderocol is preferred when susceptible for MBL Pseudomonas; aztreonam-avibactam has limited activity. 6. Does every CRE infection require two independently active drugs? Show explanation No. Routine combination therapy adds toxicity without established benefit once an active beta-lactam regimen is identified. Specific combinations such as sulbactam-durlobactam plus a carbapenem have separate rationale. 7. Is TMP-SMX monotherapy the 2026 default for invasive Stenotrophomonas? Show explanation No. Cefiderocol monotherapy is preferred in the current guidance, with explicitly limited human comparative evidence. TMP-SMX is an alternative component of combination therapy. 8. Can nitrofurantoin complete treatment of ESBL bacteremia from a urinary source? Show explanation No. Urinary activity does not provide adequate bloodstream exposure. 9. Does MRSA pneumonia respond to daptomycin? Show explanation Daptomycin should not be used for alveolar pneumonia because pulmonary surfactant inactivates it. 10. What laboratory monitoring must accompany TMP-SMX? Show explanation Potassium, renal function, and CBC, with timing based on baseline risk, dose, and treatment duration. Review interacting medications.

Show explanation No. Cefiderocol monotherapy is preferred in the current guidance, with explicitly limited human comparative evidence. TMP-SMX is an alternative component of combination therapy. 8. Can nitrofurantoin complete treatment of ESBL bacteremia from a urinary source? Show explanation No. Urinary activity does not provide adequate bloodstream exposure. 9. Does MRSA pneumonia respond to daptomycin? Show explanation Daptomycin should not be used for alveolar pneumonia because pulmonary surfactant inactivates it. 10. What laboratory monitoring must accompany TMP-SMX? Show explanation Potassium, renal function, and CBC, with timing based on baseline risk, dose, and treatment duration. Review interacting medications.

slides.title: Antibiotic resistance · One-page rounds sheet
slides.section: Antibiotic resistance · One-page rounds sheet
paragraphs: September 21, 2026 · Teaching companion; faculty/local review pending. See the full module for dosing, evidence, exceptions, and sources.
Name the syndrome, assess severity, review prior isolates, obtain appropriate cultures, and control the source. A resistant colonizer does not need antibiotics.
Invasive ESBL: carbapenem preferred. Invasive moderate-risk AmpC: active, optimized cefepime or a carbapenem when indicated. Do not transfer the cefepime rule from AmpC to ESBL.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Antibiotic resistance · One-page rounds sheet September 21, 2026 · Teaching companion; faculty/local review pending. See the full module for dosing, evidence, exceptions, and sources. Start with infection Name the syndrome, assess severity, review prior isolates, obtain appropriate cultures, and control the source. A resistant colonizer does not need antibiotics. ESBL and AmpC Invasive ESBL: carbapenem preferred. Invasive moderate-risk AmpC: active, optimized cefepime or a carbapenem when indicated. Do not transfer the cefepime rule from AmpC to ESBL. CRE mechanism KPC: meropenem-vaborbactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, or imipenem-relebactam. NDM: aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. OXA-48-like: ceftazidime-avibactam. Confirm AST. Pseudomonas Use an optimized traditional beta-lactam when appropriate and susceptible. DTR: test the four newer agents. For MBL producers, cefiderocol is preferred if active.
